dsDefects.text:
Design-system issues still open (not fixed on this canvas). The admin app ships light only for release 1.0 (owner decision), so the dark-theme items below don’t block launch.
The canvas now uses the design system’s tokens.css as published (Plus Jakarta Sans / IBM Plex Mono, dark label on the orange button, brand focus ring, real motion). Every local token override and drift banner is gone; composites.css holds only the proposed components, built from DS tokens.
• Button focus on filled buttons: .hg-on-brand / .hg-on-accent / .hg-on-danger draw the ring in --focus-on-color (#FFFFFF) on a gap in the fill colour. White ring against --surface-base #FFFAEA: 1.04:1; against --surface-raised #FFFFFF (the decision bar): 1.00:1. tokens.css now defines --focus-ring-on-brand and friends, but the Button bundle doesn’t read them, and in light they are still white.
• Dark --border-interactive (neutral 600, #6E7C77) on dark --surface-raised (#33352F): 2.85:1, under 3:1 for a control boundary (Input, Select, Checkbox, Radio, tertiary Button inside cards and panels).
• Badge neutral in dark: --text-secondary (#B9B0A0) on the fixed --color-neutral-100 tint (#F6EFDD): 1.87:1. Badge tints don’t follow the theme.
• Button ghost on --surface-chrome: --text-primary #232323 on #1B3B31 is 1.28:1. The SideNav draws Sign out as its own nav row instead.
• Density: tokens.css has compact values but no density selector, so page roots map --density-row-height and friends to --density-compact-* (owner decision: 44 px rows).
Resolved by the new tokens: the primary label is now 4.63:1 (dark forest ink on orange); fonts, focus colour and focus widths come from tokens.css.

ownerDecisions.text:
Owner decisions on this canvas
Settled (28 Sep):
• Rejecting one rider document doesn’t notify the rider; only Request changes or Reject application does. Copy says so; a Needs API tag records that the contract still shows the rejection at once.
• Table cells use the short date form; the full absolute date is in the tooltip and the detail view.
• SideNav and KeyValueList join the design system (approved, not in it yet); drawn here as proposed components.
• Desktop web layout: the page never scrolls; no overlay modals for working tasks; collapsible navigation and panes; overview → detail → more detail side by side. Applied to every board: the modal boards are now in-page panel boards at 1440 × 900 and the 1480 px scrolling board is gone.
Settled (round 2, 1 Oct):
• Support agents open a rider application only from a support case; the queue boards for support are gone and the contract narrows.
• A suspected forgery is never rejected by the reviewer: they record the matching check as Fail with a note for the Super Admin and the claim is released. Only a Super Admin decides during the hold; the page is read-only for reviewers.
• After three resubmissions, approve or reject only (drawn).
• Light theme only for release 1.0: the dark boards are gone.
• Times are 12-hour everywhere.
Still open:
• BLOCKER for build hand-off: what does Approve send as reason_code? RiderDecisionInput requires it and types it as a document rejection code, which has no approval value. Until the contract changes, Approve rider stays off (“Approval isn’t available yet.”) with a Needs API tag.

specDetail.text:
Detail behaviour
• Panes, left to right (owner rule: overview → detail → more detail, side by side; nothing overlays the work): the side navigation folds to a 56 px rail; the queue folds to a 48 px strip (Show the queue expands it); the application pane (368 px: banner, Decision readiness, Documents, Rider details); the document pane (viewer, then the checks pane, 500 px). Handles between panes resize them (proposed SplitPanes, shadcn Resizable); arrow keys resize, Enter folds or restores.
• The page never scrolls. At 1440 × 900 the scan, every check (seven for a Government ID), the note to the rider and Approve / Reject document are on screen together. A pane scrolls inside itself only if its content is longer than the viewport.
• The application’s state, attempt, review target and claim countdown sit in the app bar, so no pane loses height to them.
• Application pane sections fold to their header (proposed Disclosure): Rider details is folded while reviewing and opens for the email reveal.
• At 1024 px the application pane folds to a strip too; at 1280 px the panes narrow.
• Opening a row never claims. Deciding needs a claim from Take next, which may return a different application (DetailSwitched explains the switch).
• Buttons that open a panel carry aria-expanded and aria-controls (they open a region of the page, not a dialog). A disabled Approve rider stays focusable and is described by the bar’s reason, plus the blocker list when it is shown.
• Each document’s checks are answers sent as checks[]. Passes or Fails is required, except on checks the spec marks conditional (work-permit expiry; owner consent on a registration), which also offer “Doesn’t apply”. The age row is computed and read only. Approve document turns on when every answer passes or doesn’t apply.
• Two kinds of note, never mixed: the note to the rider (review_note, shown word for word) and each check’s internal note (recorded, never sent).
• Owner answer (28 Sep): rejecting one document only records it; the rider is told only when you send Request changes or Reject application. The contract doesn’t keep that promise yet, so the copy carries a Needs API tag (getRiderOnboardingStatus shows a document’s rejection at once).
• Viewer keys (Page Up / Page Down, + / −) work only while focus is inside the scan region, so typing in a note never zooms.
• When the last document is approved and Approve rider is still blocked (approval needs a contract change), focus goes to the decision bar’s status line, never to a disabled button. After the contract change, focus goes to the enabled Approve rider.

specDialogs.text:
Decision panel behaviour (was: dialogs)
• Owner rule for desktop web: no overlay sheets or modals for working tasks. Every decision opens as an in-page panel (proposed DetailPanel): Reject document and Super Admin override open in the checks pane, beside the scan; Reject application, Request changes, Approve rider, Super Admin reverse and release, and support re-open replace the document pane while open. The application pane and the decision bar stay visible.
• Opening moves focus to the panel title. Cancel, the close button or Escape closes it (not while sending) and returns focus to the button that opened it. No focus trap: the rest of the page stays usable. One decision panel at a time; the other decision buttons are off until it closes.
• Confirm with an invalid field keeps the panel open, shows the error under the field and moves focus to the first invalid field.
• No reason is ever preselected on a rejection, except Expired when the policy has under 14 days left. The consequence line follows the reason: fixable reasons (illegible, expired, wrong type, pages missing) say support can re-open; the rest say only a Super Admin can reverse, within 30 days.
• Reason lists are filtered by document type (see the reason note).
• The reject-document note to the rider starts empty; “Insert my note to the rider from the checks” copies the checks pane’s note in for editing. Internal check notes never reach the rider.
• If the claim ends, another reviewer decides or the application changes while a panel is open, the panel turns into “Not sent: …”, the typed message kept read only with Copy message, and one action, Reload the application.
• Attempts: riders get 3 resubmissions; the 4th rejection deactivates the account and only support can re-open it. Attempt 3: Request changes says the rider gets one last upload. Attempt 4: Reject application warns that rejecting deactivates the account.
• Neither Request changes nor Reject application offers Suspected forgery or Suspected alteration (owner decision, round 2). When “No sign of editing or forgery” fails, the reviewer flags the document: the check and a note go to a Super Admin, the claim is released, and the application is on hold and read-only until a Super Admin decides.
• Reject document turns on only once a check is marked Fails. Every rider checklist opens with “Legible, every page present”.
• Submitting: confirm shows loading, fields are read only, Escape doesn’t close. Failure keeps everything typed; Try again resends the same Idempotency-Key. Offline: nothing is queued.
• Approve rider opens its panel only once the contract allows an approval without a rejection code. Until then the bar’s Approve rider is off with “Approval isn’t available yet.” and a Needs API tag.

specQueue.text:
Queue behaviour
• Layout (owner rule for desktop web): the working page never scrolls. The grid is a LyteNyte grid that virtualises inside its own region; the page stays still. Opening a row (Enter) opens the application in a pane beside the list, never an overlay, and never claims it.
• Take next is a POST with an Idempotency-Key: the button shows loading, ignores repeat presses, and a retry reuses the key, so it can never claim two. Its helper sits beside it (“Claims the oldest unclaimed application for 60 minutes. Opening a row only reads it.”) and describes it, so a disabled Take next still gives its reason.
• Order is fixed, oldest first (no sort parameter; the rider onboarding spec makes the queue first in, first out).
• The only server filter is onboarding state (several at once). One empty state for the default filter (“Nothing waiting for review” + Show all states). “Nothing to take” is a result banner after Take next returns nothing, never an empty-table state; when rows remain it explains they are all claimed and when the first claim ends.
• Dates (owner answer, 28 Sep): table cells use the short form (26 Sep, 5:55 pm; the year only when it isn’t this year). The full absolute date shows in a tooltip on the cell and in the detail view.
• The count line and the nav count use the page total only when the server sends it; otherwise “Showing N · more below” and no nav count.
• Two-line cells: 18 px + 16 px (body-sm, the 13 px floor) inside the 44 px compact row (owner decision: compact 44 px rows).
• Names are display_name exactly as sent. States before Documents review read “Not submitted yet” (Needs API: meaning of submitted_at before submission).
• A row whose claim expired reads “Unclaimed (previous claim ended …)”, with no lock icon.

specReasons.text:
Rejection reasons by document type (rider)
• Never offered for riders: Address doesn’t match (a rider profile has no address) and Issuer not recognised (the halal-certifier reason).
• Government ID, driver’s licence: Illegible, Expired, Wrong document type, Name doesn’t match, Date of birth doesn’t match, Suspected forgery, Suspected alteration, Pages missing, Other.
• Vehicle registration, vehicle insurance: Illegible, Expired, Wrong document type, Name doesn’t match, Plate doesn’t match, Suspected forgery, Suspected alteration, Pages missing, Other.
• Work eligibility: Illegible, Expired, Wrong document type, Name doesn’t match, Date of birth doesn’t match, Suspected forgery, Suspected alteration, Pages missing, Other.
• Profile photo: Illegible, Wrong document type, Suspected alteration, Other.
• Suspected forgery and Suspected alteration are offered only in the flag panel, after “No sign of editing or forgery” fails; they put the application on hold for a Super Admin and are never a reviewer’s rejection (owner decision, round 2).
• Reject application and Request changes: the union for the rider’s vehicle type, without Suspected forgery and Suspected alteration (Plate doesn’t match only when the vehicle has a plate).
• Other needs a 20-character note on a document rejection. The application message is always 10 to 1,000 characters.
